observations: Several white woven polypropylene sacks, tied shut, apparently containing coiled cable, stacked on a concrete/tiled floor
A large loose coil of insulated cable with blue and black outer jackets, multi-strand, on the right
A smaller coil of orange/copper-colored insulated cable, bottom left
A dark (black) coil of cable in front
A white plastic item (possibly a junction box or pipe fitting) in the foreground, unrelated to the cable
No cut cross-section of any cable is visible, so the conductor metal (aluminium vs copper vs copper-clad-aluminium) cannot be seen
No scale, tag, or weight indicator visible in the photo

claims.claim: Aluminium cable scrap (end-of-life electrical wiring, power cables, and industrial cabling)
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows only the outer insulation/jacket of the coils and sacks; no cut end exposes the bare conductor strands, so the metal type cannot be confirmed from the image.

risks.risk: Conductor metal may not be aluminium (could be copper, copper-clad-aluminium, or steel-cored), which changes scrap value drastically
risks.proof: Close-up photo or clip of a freshly cut cable end on each bundle type, showing bare metal strand color and texture
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lowest-value plausible metal (aluminium) rather than copper

risks.risk: Cable is still insulated/jacketed, not stripped bare, which lowers per-kg scrap value versus bare wire
risks.proof: Photo already shows jackets intact; would need a stripped sample photo to show bare wire content ratio
risks.if_unproven: priced as insulated/un-stripped scrap, not bare wire

risks.risk: Total weight of the lot is unknown; scrap is normally priced by kilogram
risks.proof: Photo or video of the bundles on a weighing scale with the reading visible
risks.if_unproven: priced at the minimum plausible weight visible in the photo, pending scale confirmation

risks.risk: Contents of the closed white sacks are unseen; they may contain non-cable material, offcuts, or mixed junk reducing average value
risks.proof: Photo of sacks opened showing the cable inside each one
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming lowest-value mixed scrap content inside sacks

risks.risk: Possible contamination with non-metal waste (plastic, wood, dirt) increasing apparent weight without value
risks.proof: Close-up photo of a sample bundle interior
risks.if_unproven: priced net of estimated contamination deduction

proof_requests: Photo/video of a freshly cut cable end for each distinct coil/sack type, showing bare conductor color
Photo of the lot on a weighing scale with the display visible
Photo of the inside of at least one closed sack
Any purchase/scrap yard receipt or certificate indicating metal grade, if available
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as bundled insulated scrap cable, but the seller's aluminium claim cannot be confirmed from the photo since no cut end reveals the conductor; per rules this unproven claim and the unknown weight are priced at worst case rather than blocking a price.
